newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Straddles bought in Glaxo Wellcome.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Straddles bought in Glaxo Wellcome.

text.p: An opportunity to buy volatility in pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome was taken in the UK traded options market as traders either bought straddles or straight calls as the main deals on Monday, dealers said.
The largest stock options deal by the afternoon was from a buyer of 500 October 1200 puts and calls in Glaxo at 47p and 63p each.
Increased implied volatility would help the straddle make a profit and if the position is held to expiry, a profit will be made if the stock either goes below 1090p or above 1310p.
By 1420 GMT, Glaxo shares were up 2p to 1202-1/2p.
Taking advantage of the recent share price slide in Glaxo was a buyer of 240 October 1350 calls at 15p.

In contrast, the main deals in gas distributor Centrica were from sellers of call options. One deal was to sell 500 September 70 calls followed by a further sale of 480 lots, both at 18p. Centrica shares added 1-1/4p to 89p.

Trading was mixed in FTSE 100 index options as the market attempted to recover from its initial fall. This did not deter one trader from buying 500 September 4300 puts at 13p betting the market will drop back again before the expiry date. Taking the opposite view was a buyer of 300 October 4900 calls at 157p.

More complex was a call spread, which was hedged by buying FTSE futures in a volatility trade. The deal was to sell 500 December 4700 calls at 341-1/2p and to buy 500 December 5125 calls at 122p making a net credit of 219-1/2p against buying September futures at 4835.

If futures prices fall or stabilise, more call spreads may be sold to produce a profit and if the futures rise, losses from the spread will limit profits. By 1420 GMT, September futures were up 15 at 4862, while cash FTSE was down 14.0 at 4851.8.
